slice.source_qualification: official repository documentation pinned to an exact commit
slice.tested_scope: Only the documented semantics of cargo fetch, --offline, --locked and --frozen in the pinned cargo-fetch command page; no Cargo execution, no second public source, and no broader cache implementation claims.
slice.finding: The pinned Cargo documentation states that cargo fetch downloads git and registry dependencies so they are locally available, and that subsequent Cargo commands can run offline after a fetch unless Cargo.lock changes. It also states that --offline prevents network access and restricts resolution to locally downloaded crates, while --frozen combines --locked and --offline.
slice.phase1_interpretation: This is positive evidence for a deterministic local-cache reuse pattern with enforceable no-network use-time behavior after dependencies are populated. It is not a strict Chat-parity pass because the initial fetch itself is a networked dependency-population step and no Chat-exposed zero-executor mechanism for performing that population was established in this slice.
slice.scope_guard: Do not infer that every Cargo command will succeed offline, that vendoring is equivalent to fetch, that cache population is Chat-native, or that end-to-end richer-mode outcome parity is solved. The docs explicitly condition offline reuse on locally downloaded dependencies and an unchanged lock file, and warn offline resolution may differ from online mode.
